_about: Rules, thresholds and procedures the operators state in their own Operations blog (75 articles read on 2026-11-07, Dec 2017 to Oct 2026; extracted by model readers, quotes up to 25 words). Evidence for hypotheses, not parsed data; nothing here feeds the model.

rules.title: Winds & Lift Operations at Squaw
rules.statement: If anemometer reads 120mph, they will not try to move lifts; at 20-50mph they go to the lift, run it and observe
rules.quote: If it is reporting 120mph we're not even going to try and move lifts

rules.title: Winds & Lift Operations at Squaw
rules.statement: Wind speed and direction determine whether a lift can operate (lift/wind vulnerability chart)
rules.quote: We use wind direction and intensity to determine whether a lift can operate or not.

rules.title: Winds & Lift Operations at Squaw
rules.statement: Chair swing within manufacturer-approved limit (front-back and side-side) is the basis of the decision to run a chair
rules.quote: Majority of the decisions to operate is based on the chair swing.

rules.title: Winds & Lift Operations at Squaw
rules.statement: Gusty winds worsen chair swing; steady moderate winds more predictable, but steady high winds often still prevent safe operation
rules.quote: Gusty winds are bad because it pushes and creates more turbulence while increasing chair swing.

rules.title: Winds & Lift Operations at Squaw
rules.statement: NWS forecast is considered; if winds already high and forecast to increase, lift may be closed; if marginal and forecast to decrease, wait and put lift on wind hold
rules.quote: we will wait and watch to see if we can open that lift and put it on 'wind hold'

rules.title: Operations Update: Nov 27
rules.statement: Rime removal: crews stop each chair in top and bottom terminals and remove ice from every grip on detachable lifts; all grips must be completely cleared
rules.quote: These all need to be completely cleared of ice in order to operate.

rules.title: Operations Update: Nov 27
rules.statement: Funitel saw no ice; Aerial Tram ice only at top terminal High Camp (8200 ft)
rules.quote: Funitel saw no ice build up and the Aerial Tram only saw ice build up at the top terminal

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: Patrol teams work up to 49 avalanche mitigation routes on a snow safety day; must wait for daylight; each route 30 min to 2 hours; some routes depend on prior routes; whole program can take a full day or more
rules.quote: Patrollers start their work day as early as 5am, they must wait until the sun rises and it's light out

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: Squaw Valley has 28 mitigation routes in five avalanche complexes; Alpine has 21 routes including Alpine Meadows Road
rules.quote: There are 28 avalanche mitigation routes spread out among these five complexes at Squaw Valley.

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: Gazex cannons fired before first routes of the day, and possibly again at end of day to maintain access for grooming crews
rules.quote: Gazex cannons are fired before patrol teams start their first routes of the day

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: No chairlifts at either resort can open after a large storm without avalanche control, including First Venture (needs Poulsen's Gully mitigation) and Subway and Meadow at Alpine
rules.quote: neither resort includes lifts that can operate after significant snowfall without first performing avalanche hazard mitigation

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: Extreme wind combined with high snowfall intensity reduces visibility and hinders mitigation; winds over 100mph described as routine
rules.quote: Winds in excess of 100mph are routine, and can be strong enough to knock a patroller over.

rules.title: Avalanche Hazard Mitigation at Squaw Alpine
rules.statement: Alpine uses a 105mm Howitzer about 12 times per season under Forest Service special use permit; Squaw Valley is on private land and not eligible for the artillery program
rules.quote: 105mm Howitzer (on average 12 times per season)

rules.title: Operations Update: Heavy Snowfall & What to Expect
rules.statement: Rime ice: every detachable chair has 40 to 80 grips, each banged by hand 5-30 times to break ice
rules.quote: Every detachable chair on both mountains has 40 to 80 grips, and each grip has to get banged on 5-30 times by hand

rules.title: Operations Update: Heavy Snowfall & What to Expect
rules.statement: After 1 inch per hour snowfall, avalanche hazards considered very high
rules.quote: after 1" per hour, the avalanche hazards are considered to be very high

rules.title: Operations Update: Heavy Snowfall & What to Expect
rules.statement: Chairs bumped overnight where possible; chairs removed from KT-22 line overnight to prevent icing; avalanche control done daily when safe
rules.quote: we will be bumping chairs overnight where possible and maintaining avalanche control routes

rules.title: Operations Update: Heavy Snowfall & What to Expect
rules.statement: Funitel/Tram run if wind slows enough to access upper mountain lifts for avalanche control
rules.quote: If we experience a slowdown in wind and can access upper mountain lifts to perform avalanche control, we will run them.

rules.title: Operations Update: Some Lifts Still Frozen, Winds Surprised Us Today

rules.title: Operations Update: Some Lifts Still Frozen, Winds Surprised Us Today

rules.title: Operations Blog: Winds Created Rime Ice; Busy Weekend Ahead
rules.statement: Every piece of ice must be removed from lift grips; any ice remaining means the lift cannot run
rules.quote: If any ice whatsoever is still on the grip... the lift cannot run.

rules.title: Operations Blog: Winds Created Rime Ice; Busy Weekend Ahead
rules.statement: Behind-the-scenes work continues during holds: grooming roads, maintaining avalanche control routes, de-icing lifts
rules.quote: We are still grooming roads, maintaining avalanche control routes, and de-icing lifts wherever possible.

rules.title: Operations Update: Deep Dive on Wind Hold & Other Storm Updates
rules.statement: Lift Maintenance Director (Chris Woo) considers 5 factors for wind hold: anemometer readings and physical testing, wind speed and direction, chair swing, wind frequency (gusty vs steady), and forecast. Interview said to be a few years old but process unchanged.
rules.quote: This interview with Chris is from a few years ago, but the way we assess for wind hold has not changed.

rules.title: Operations Update: Deep Dive on Wind Hold & Other Storm Updates
rules.statement: If anemometer reports 120mph lifts are not tried; at 20-50mph they go to the lift, run it and observe
rules.quote: If it is reporting 120mph we're not even going to try and move lifts

rules.quote: There is an approved chair swing by the manufacturer

rules.title: Operations Update: Deep Dive on Wind Hold & Other Storm Updates
rules.statement: Gusty winds are worse than steady moderate winds; steady high winds still often prevent safe operation
rules.quote: Gusty winds are bad because it pushes and creates more turbulence while increasing chair swing.

rules.quote: a chair hit a tower, which also triggers an automatic shut-down

rules.title: Operations Update: Deep Dive on Wind Hold & Other Storm Updates
rules.statement: Many popular lifts sit directly on the Sierra Crest
rules.quote: many of our most popular chairlifts are situated directly on the Sierra Crest
